comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Phase 1 interim — reconciler failure isolated to a single Jira issue at its comment cap

**The reconciler is healthy in every respect except one issue.** Auth, acli, the runner, and
the workflow are all fine: every other mutation in every failing run reports `error=None`.

**Failing chain (identical in all runs sampled):**

1. `acli jira workitem comment create --key REB-1861 --body ...` is rejected by Jira with
   `io.atlassian.micros.clibackend.exceptions.CLIBackendException: COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: 5000`
   — REB-1861 has reached Jira's hard cap of 5000 comments per issue.
2. acli **exits 0** while reporting FAILURE, so `_check_mutation_failure` raises
   `AcliMutationError` (`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:345`).
3. Each `add_comment` failure is individually non-fatal and captured into `comment_errors`
   (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:383`), but they aggregate into a single failing batch outcome:
   `RECON: batch_outcome action=update key=REB-1861 error='comment-errors: ...'`
4. That one failing mutation trips the operational-failure exit
   (`rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:476`):
   `ERROR: reconcile completed with 1 mutation failures` -> `Reconcile failed (exit 1)`.
5. Because the comment never lands, the outbound differ recomputes it as still-missing on the
   next pass and re-emits it. The failure is therefore **permanent, not transient** — it cannot
   self-clear.

**Evidence — deterministic, not a flake.** Identical signature in the first failing run and in
the latest:

| Run | Time (UTC) | Cap error | Failing mutations | Sole failing key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32340215770 | 06:35 | — | — | (SUCCESS — last green) |
| 32344687307 | 07:35 | `...LIMIT_EXCEEDED: 5000` | 1 | REB-1861 |
| 32369587520 | 12:34 | `...LIMIT_EXCEEDED: 5000` | 1 | REB-1861 |
| 32398224961 | 17:33 | `...LIMIT_EXCEEDED: 5000` | 1 | REB-1861 |

**ACs 2 — candidate causes ruled out by this evidence:**

- *Workflow disabled* — RULED OUT: the workflow dispatches on schedule every hour and runs
  10-16 minutes.
- *Runner outage* — RULED OUT: checkout, Python setup, acli install, and ~1200 invariant scans
  all complete normally.
- *acli auth / Jira credentials* — RULED OUT: 53 outbound updates and 3 typed inbound
  dispatches apply successfully in the same pass; only the capped issue is rejected, and it is
  rejected on a **quota** error, not an auth error.
- *Reconciler error* — CONFIRMED, with the precise mechanism above.

**Not a regression from a code change in the window.** Commits landing between the last green
(06:35Z) and first red (07:35Z) were documentation/test changes with no reconciler-path effect.
The trigger is a **data threshold crossing** — REB-1861 accumulating its 5000th comment — hitting
a code path that has **no guard for the per-issue comment-count cap**.

**Structural precedent.** rebar already fixed the *sibling* bug for the comment **length** cap
(Jira's 32,767-char body limit) under bug `6afc-20ee-84e5-4dd5`, with a shared truncation helper
at `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` applied to BOTH the send path and the differ's comparison
path so the two converge. Its module docstring describes this exact failure shape verbatim:

> "acli ... exits 0 even when the underlying Jira operation fails ... the comment never lands.
> Because the outbound differ decides a comment needs adding when the local body is *not present*
> in Jira, the never-landed comment is re-emitted on every reconciler pass."

The **count** cap is the same failure mode against a different Jira limit, and it currently has
no equivalent guard. Analysis of the correct seam and the fix/no-fix disposition follows.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Phase 1 — mechanism fully traced to the exit-1 seam (two independent promoters)

Follow-up to the previous comment. The path from "Jira refuses the comment" to "workflow exits
1" runs through **two** independent promoters, both riding one env flag that this workflow
turns on.

**`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:288` sets `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP: "1"`.**
Per `docs/config.md:354-363` that flag is the **silent-no-op canary** (epic f89d / story 2359),
default off => warn-first; set to `1` it promotes a detection to a hard per-mutation failure.
Bug 48c8-5375-f883-462d later hung a *second* promoter on the same flag.

Both now fire on REB-1861:

1. **Swallowed-comment-failure promotion** (`apply_handlers.py:407-416`, bug 48c8) — fires on
   ANY non-empty `comment_errors`, setting `outcome["error"] = "comment-errors: ..."`.
2. **Silent-no-op canary** (bug 3f04) — fires when `computed > 0 && applied == 0`.

Observed transition across the incident, from the batch outcomes:

| Run | Time (UTC) | comments_applied | add_comment failures | silent_noop | Promoters firing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32344687307 | 07:35 | 7 | 32 | `[]` | 48c8 only |
| 32398224961 | 17:33 | 0 | 39 | `['comments']` | 48c8 **and** 3f04 |

The 07:35 run is the moment REB-1861 **crossed** the cap: 7 comments landed (filling it to
exactly 5000), the remaining 32 were refused. From then on nothing lands, so the canary joins in.

**The backlog grows and can never drain** — 32 un-landable comments at 07:35Z, 39 at 17:33Z.
Local comments keep accruing; Jira can accept none of them; the outbound differ recomputes the
whole un-landed set every pass because a comment is considered "needs adding" when its body is
not present in Jira. This is the *identical* convergence-failure shape documented in
`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` for the comment-**length** cap (bug 6afc-20ee-84e5-4dd5) — same
mechanism, different Jira limit, and the **count** limit has no guard anywhere in `src/`.

**Consequence for any fix: classifying the comment error alone is NOT sufficient.** Suppressing
`comment_errors` would silence promoter 1 but leave promoter 2 (`applied == 0`) still reddening
the run. The codebase already documents the correct handling for exactly this situation, at
`dispatch_apply_phases.py:188-196`:

> "Callers must skip WITHOUT incrementing their `*_computed`/`*_applied` counters: those feed
> `apply_handlers`' silent-no-op canary, which is a FAILURE detector ... and routing a DESIGNED
> skip through it would re-conflate exactly what this guard separates."

So the precedented shape is the **skip-vs-failure split** (ticket a3fa, `pass_io.record_capability_gap`)
and the hierarchy-rejection precedent (`dispatch_one.py:525-558`, tickets 8b25/39c1): a permanent
platform refusal that no retry can fix is a **designed skip** — WARN, record a durable
`bridge_alerts` entry so the divergence stays visible, do **not** reach `comment_errors`, and do
**not** increment the sub-op counters.

**Repo code vs environment — the answer is BOTH, and they need different owners:**

- **Environment / data (not fixable in code):** REB-1861 has permanently exhausted Jira's
  5000-comment cap. rebar cannot un-fill it, and there is **no config escape hatch** — nothing in
  `docs/config.md` or `src/rebar/config` lets an operator exclude one issue from comment sync.
- **Repo code (the defect):** rebar classifies a permanent, un-retryable platform quota refusal as
  a per-mutation failure, which reds the whole hourly bridge. That contradicts the project's own
  documented skip-vs-failure invariant cited above.

Ruled out again by this evidence: auth/credentials (7 comments landed in the same pass; the
refusal is a quota error, not a 401/403), runner outage, and workflow-disabled.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE FOUND — and it is NOT the comment cap. The bridge is duplicating comments into Jira every hour.

The 5000-comment cap is a **consequence**, not the cause. The cause is that the outbound
comment differ never recognises already-synced comments as present, so it **re-posts the same
comments to Jira on every hourly pass**. REB-1861 is simply the first issue to fill up.

### The decisive evidence

REB-1861 maps to local ticket `5200-e04e-246e-4aae` (`nonmystic-topiary-toadfish`) — a **closed**
story with **40 local comments**. Jira holds **5000**. A 125x divergence that no legitimate
activity explains.

Then the discriminating test: compare per-issue pending/applied comment counts between the
07:35Z run and the 17:33Z run — **ten passes apart, on closed tickets with no new local
comments.** If the sync converged, these would be zero after the first pass.

| Jira key | local ticket | status | local comments | pending 07:35 | pending 17:33 | applied 07:35 | applied 17:33 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REB-1580 | adroit-deductible-kakapo | closed | 24 | 21 | 21 | **21** | **21** |
| REB-1570 | fireless-schematic-gadwall | closed | 25 | 8 | 8 | **8** | **8** |
| REB-424 | orb-mantle-talon | closed | 25 | 3 | 3 | **3** | **3** |
| REB-1861 | nonmystic-topiary-toadfish | closed | 40 | 39 | 39 | 7 then 0 (cap) | 0 (cap) |

The counts are **identical ten hours later**, and `comments_applied` equals `pending` — so those
comments **successfully land in Jira on every single pass and are posted again the next hour**.
This is not a stalled queue; it is an active duplication loop. The differ decides a comment
"needs adding" when its body is not found in Jira, and for these comments that test never
becomes true even immediately after a successful post.

### Scale of the ongoing corruption

From the 17:33Z pass alone:

- **205 comments re-posted into Jira in one pass**, across **28 issues**.
- At the hourly cadence that is **~4,920 duplicate Jira comments per day**.
- REB-1861 re-emits 39/pass; 5000 / 39 ~= 128 passes ~= 5.3 days of hourly running to fill the cap
  — consistent with it tipping over on 2026-08-20.
- Top re-emitters right now: REB-1861 (39), REB-1580 (21), REB-1829 (18), REB-3067 (15),
  REB-2823 (15), REB-2882 (13), REB-1563 (13), REB-2213 (12).

**This is progressive and will keep claiming issues.** REB-1580 at 21/pass reaches the 5000 cap
in roughly ten days, then it too reds the bridge. Fixing only the cap-error classification would
silence the alarm while leaving the duplication running.

### Correction to my earlier comments

My first two comments correctly traced the *failure* path (cap refusal ->
`comment_errors` + silent-no-op canary -> `mutation_failures` -> exit 1) and that analysis stands
as the mechanism by which the red run is produced. But the *originating* defect is upstream of
all of it: comment-sync idempotency is broken. A guard for the per-issue count cap remains a
legitimate hardening item, but it is **not** the fix for this incident.

### Answer to "repo code or environment"

**Repo code.** Nothing about credentials, the runner, acli, or the workflow is at fault — 205
comments authenticate and post successfully every pass. The defect is in rebar's outbound
comment-diff / comment-id-recording path, which fails to mark landed comments as landed.

### Scope

This is materially larger than the filed bug (a red workflow) and involves ongoing writes to
production Jira. Escalating to the operator before any code change: the duplication loop, not
the cap, is what needs fixing, and stopping the bleed may warrant pausing the bridge first.

comments.body:
## Discovered work filed — and why this ticket is BLOCKED on it

Filed `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (`aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`, P1 bug), linked `discovered_from` this ticket:
**"Outbound comment sync is not idempotent — ~205 comments re-posted to Jira every hourly pass"**.

That is the real defect. This canary ticket cannot go green until it is fixed, because the cap
refusal on REB-1861 is produced by the duplication loop and will keep being produced.

**No code change has been made.** The remediation is materially larger than this bug's scope and
involves ongoing writes to production Jira, so it is escalated to the operator for a decision
before anything is implemented. Two candidate scopes, deliberately kept separate:

1. **Fix the duplication loop** (`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker`) — the actual cause. Needs runtime
   evidence first to establish which dedup layer fails; do not fix from static reading.
2. **Harden the cap classification** (separate, optional) — treat `COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`
   as a designed skip rather than a per-mutation failure, per the project's own skip-vs-failure
   split (ticket a3fa) and the hierarchy-rejection precedent (`dispatch_one.py:525-558`). This
   would make the bridge green again **without** fixing the duplication — which is why it must not
   be done alone: it would silence the alarm while ~4,920 duplicate comments/day keep landing.

**Operator decision needed:** whether to pause reconcile-bridge.yml to stop the bleed while the
idempotency fix is developed. Every hour it runs adds ~205 duplicate comments across 28 issues and
pushes the next issue (REB-1580, ~10 days out) toward the same cap.

This ticket stays open and claimed; it auto-closes on the next successful reconcile-bridge run.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Root cause pinned to production state — see `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` for the full evidence

Direct inspection of the live binding store (`git show origin/tickets:.bridge_state/bindings.json`)
shows the comment-ID dedup map is **empty**:

```
bindings entries:      2475
comment_ids ENTRIES:      0
```

Zero entries after thousands of successfully posted comments. The PRIMARY dedup skip
(`binding_store.is_comment_mapped(local_comment_key)`, `outbound_comments.py:411-415`) therefore
**can never fire**, leaving only the SECONDARY body-equality test — which the code itself
describes as a belt-and-suspenders guard for a lost map write. That test compares a locally
fitted+normalized body against bodies that round-tripped through ADF/wiki conversion, so rich
comments never match and are re-posted every hour, forever. REB-1861's comments are the richest
in the affected set (40 local, avg 3.6 KB, heavy markdown) and match at **1 of 40** — which is why
it filled Jira's 5000-comment cap first and reds this workflow.

**Ruled out:** the previously-fixed pagination route (bug `1f3d-cb66-d3fc-4356`,
`florid-vigorous-urial`) is NOT regressed — `get_comments` correctly uses `--paginate`
(`acli_cli_ops.py:583-600`) and the snapshot truncation guard is in place
(`outbound_comments.py:322-346`). This is the same failure class arriving by a different route.
Its cleanup task `bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` is the established precedent for purging duplicates
afterward.

Still unconfirmed and deliberately not fixed from static reading: which of the four silent
no-op guards in `_record_comment_id` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:309-334`) leaves the map empty.
That requires instrumenting a live pass and is AC 1 on `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker`.

No code change made; awaiting the operator's decision on scope and on whether to pause the
workflow to stop the ~205 duplicate comments/pass.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Bridge DELIBERATELY paused — this alarm is expected until further notice

`reconcile-bridge.yml` was disabled by operator decision (`gh workflow disable`, now
`disabled_manually`) at the time of this comment. **This canary will keep reporting stale until
it is re-enabled. That is expected and is not a new fault.**

### Why

The bridge was failing every hourly run AND re-posting roughly 205 duplicate comments per pass
across ~28 Jira issues (~4,920/day). Root cause is confirmed and filed as
`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (`aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615`, P1): the PRIMARY comment-dedup skip
`binding_store.is_comment_mapped(local_comment_key)` is inert in production because the
`comment_ids` map is empty —

```
git show origin/tickets:.bridge_state/bindings.json
  bindings:     2475 entries
  comment_ids:     0 entries
```

— leaving only the lossy body-equality fallback, which never matches richly-formatted comments.
REB-1861 matched 1 of 40 and filled Jira's 5000-comment cap, which is what reds this canary.

The bridge was net-negative: its sync already failed every run, while the duplicates it posted
are durable and require manual cleanup. Pausing stopped accumulating damage at the cost of sync
that was not working anyway.

### What must happen before re-enabling

1. `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` lands (root cause under `/rebar-debug` now — the open question is
   which of the four silent guards in `_record_comment_id` leaves the map empty).
2. The already-posted duplicates are remediated, following the `bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` precedent.
3. Re-enable with `gh workflow enable reconcile-bridge.yml` — an operator decision, not an
   automatic consequence of the fix landing.

This ticket auto-closes when the next successful reconcile-bridge run is detected, so it will
close on its own once the bridge is fixed and re-enabled. No action needed on it directly.

Follow-up `marshy-chummy-coot` (`2399-5e49-6b28-4d59`) tracks root-causing how the defect
escaped review, tests and CI.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Session handoff — the underlying incident is RESOLVED; this canary needs re-evaluation

State at handoff: `in_progress`. This is a heartbeat canary, not a defect ticket, and the
condition that fired it has been fixed and verified.

**What happened since the pause comment above.** The bridge was deliberately disabled by operator
decision while the duplicate-comment incident was root-caused. That work completed:

- Root cause proven and fixed — `_record_comment_id`'s guard fired on the Cloud/ACLI batch
  envelope, so `comment_ids` was empty (0 bindings vs 2475 expected).
- Cleanup completed across 33 issues, verified against pre-deletion backups with zero distinct
  bodies lost.
- **Bridge re-enabled and confirmed healthy on four independent measures**: `comment_ids` 0 -> 303,
  outbound posts 251 -> 14 -> 1, the `computed=N applied=0` signature absent, and five consecutive
  successful runs.

**What the next session should do:** confirm the bridge is still running green, then close this
canary — it fired correctly, and its condition no longer holds. If it is still alarming, that is a
NEW finding and deserves its own investigation rather than being appended here; the mechanism
above is fixed and re-verified, so a fresh alarm means something else.

Do not close it on the strength of this comment alone — re-check the live state first. A canary
closed on stale evidence is worse than one left open.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Verification-then-close: alarm condition cleared; the defect lives in aa7b-5e47

Re-checked the LIVE state before closing, as the handoff comment required (not closed on the handoff alone):

- The underlying defect — outbound comment sync not idempotent, comment_ids dedup map never populated — was extracted to bug `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` (aa7b-5e47-6d3d-4615), which is now **closed**. This ticket's own comments record the recovery: root cause fixed, cleanup across 33 issues verified against backups, bridge re-enabled, `comment_ids` 0 -> 303, outbound posts 251 -> 14 -> 1, five consecutive green runs.
- Live re-check (2026-08-21 ~17:30Z, `gh run list --workflow=reconcile-bridge.yml`): the two most recent scheduled runs succeeded (32498339191 @ 15:34Z, 32503636020 @ 16:34Z). Latest success is ~1h old, so the canary condition (no success within 4h) does NOT currently hold.
- NEW, separate observation recorded for the operator: three runs earlier today (32482642367 @ 12:35Z, 32487786991 @ 13:37Z, 32492914442 @ 14:34Z) failed with a DIFFERENT mechanism — reconcile completed (`BRIDGE_STATE: converged`, all batch_outcome error=None) but the final push of the tickets branch was rejected `! [rejected] HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)`. That is a push race on the tickets ref, NOT the duplication defect this canary tracked. Per the handoff's own instruction, a fresh alarm is a new finding deserving its own investigation, not an append here — noting it so it is not lost; it has since self-cleared (two green runs after).

Closing: this canary fired correctly, its firing condition no longer holds, and the defect it surfaced is fixed and closed in aa7b-5e47.

## Reproduction Steps

The Reconciler Heartbeat Canary (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml) detected that
reconcile-bridge.yml has not completed a successful run within the
4-hour window (bridge cadence: hourly). Inspect the Actions tab.

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** reconcile-bridge.yml completes a successful run at least once
  every 4h.
- **Actual:** Reconciler unhealthy — canonical status is FAILED.
- **First red canary run:** 2026-08-20T08:11:07Z
- **Detected at:** 2026-08-20T10:07:35Z (second consecutive red canary run)
- **Canary run:** https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/32357300434

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] reconcile-bridge.yml is running and its most recent run succeeded.
- [ ] Root cause identified (workflow disabled / runner outage / acli auth /
      Jira creds / reconciler error) and addressed.

This ticket auto-closes when the next successful reconcile-bridge run is detected.
